draft.title: DC motors
card: A coil of wire sits between the poles of a magnet and carries a current. The two sides of the coil carry current in opposite directions, so the forces on them are opposite. This turns the coil.

A split ring commutator is a ring cut into two halves, joined to the ends of the coil. Each half touches a fixed brush. Every half turn it swaps which end of the coil connects to which brush, so the current in the coil reverses.
Without the commutator, the coil would swing to the vertical position, where the forces no longer turn it, and stop. With it, the forces keep turning the coil in the same direction.
The torque (turning effect) on the coil rises with more current, a stronger magnetic field or more loops of wire in the coil.
draft.remember: The commutator reverses the current each half turn so the coil keeps turning. Torque rises with current, field and loops.

a.q: What does the split ring commutator do in a DC motor?
opts: Reverses the coil's current every half turn
Changes the supply from DC to AC
Makes the magnetic field reverse each half turn
Stops the coil from moving past the vertical
a.why: Reversing the current every half turn keeps the forces on each side of the coil turning it the same way. The commutator does not change the magnet. Without the reversal, the coil would stop at the vertical position, not turn past it.
a.clue: Think about what must swap each half turn to keep the forces pushing the same way.

b.q: Ravi builds a simple DC motor in his school workshop. He wants the coil to turn with more torque, and he changes only one thing. Which change does this?
opts: Winding more loops of wire into the coil
Fitting a commutator with more brushes
Turning the magnets so the poles are swapped
Making the coil spin faster by hand at the start
b.why: More loops means the force acts on more lengths of wire, so torque rises. Swapping the poles only reverses the direction of turning. It does not change the size of the torque.
b.clue: Torque depends on current, field strength and number of loops.

a.best: Reverses the coil's current every half turn

b.best: Winding more loops of wire into the coil
